title: Describing people: personality words
lessonNotes: Use personality adjectives to describe yourself and other people.
Keep the difference clear: funny describes a person; fun describes an activity or experience.
Use evidence in a short description: kind people help others; a hardworking person works a lot.

sections.label: Grammar: be + adjective
sections.intro: Use be + an adjective to describe personality. Add a noun only when you need it: She is shy. / She is a shy person.

rules.label: Describing one person
rules.body: Use he / she + is + adjective. Do not put a before the adjective alone.

rules.label: Describing more than one person
rules.body: Use we / you / they + are + adjective.

rules.label: fun and funny
rules.body: Funny describes someone or something that makes people laugh. Fun describes an enjoyable activity, place or experience.

sections.label: Grammar exercises
sections.intro: Choose an answer. Re-read the rule, then try again if necessary.

sections.label: Vocabulary flashcards

items.explanation: Kind and easy to talk to.
Caring and helpful to other people.
Respectful and well-mannered in speech and actions.
items.example: He is polite and says please and thank you.

items.explanation: Working with a lot of effort.
items.example: Mert is hardworking; he finishes his tasks.

items.explanation: Not wanting to work or make an effort.
items.example: The lazy cat sleeps all day.

items.explanation: Having many new and original ideas.
items.example: Her creative poster uses bright shapes.

items.explanation: Nervous or quiet when talking to new people.
items.example: He is shy at first, but friendly later.

items.explanation: Serious means not joking much; funny means making people laugh.
items.example: Our teacher is serious, but her stories are funny.

sections.label: Listening: talking about other people
sections.sourceLabel: British Council LearnEnglish — A1: Talking about other people
sections.body: Open the video, complete the preparation activity, and listen for the phrases used to describe another person. The source includes a transcript and its own practice tasks. Then complete the quick checks below.

questions.prompt: In the video, which phrase is used to describe Anya positively?
choices: She's very good at her job.
questions.explanation: Listen for Yuna's description of Anya.

questions.prompt: Which structure can you use to describe a person?
questions.explanation: Use be + adjective: She is kind / friendly / creative.

sections.label: Reading: two classmates
sections.body: Mina and Can are in the same art club. Mina is friendly and creative. She has new ideas for every poster, and she helps new students feel welcome. Can is hardworking and polite. He arrives early and always says thank you when someone helps him. Mina is a little shy in large groups, but she is funny with her close friends. They are different people, but they work well together because they listen to each other.
sections.prompt: Read for the main idea first. Then find the adjective and the evidence that supports it.

questions.prompt: Why is Mina described as creative?
choices: She has new ideas for every poster.
She is in a sports club.
questions.explanation: The text gives new ideas as evidence for creative.
The text directly describes Can as hardworking and polite.

questions.prompt: Are Mina and Can the same in every way?
choices: No, but they work well together.
questions.explanation: The text says they are different people but work well together.

quiz.prompt: Which word describes a person who has many new ideas?
quiz.explanation: Creative people have new or original ideas.

choices: My friend is fun. He tells great jokes.
My friend is funny. He tells great jokes.
My friend is funny. The party is funny.
My friend is funnily. He tells jokes.
quiz.explanation: Funny describes someone who makes people laugh.
Kind people care about and help others.
Hardworking and lazy have opposite meanings.

quiz.prompt: Which word means respectful and well-mannered?
quiz.explanation: Polite means respectful in the way you speak and act.
